evidence: Path and scale follow the film: frames 1-8 boat right of center and small in both; frames 9-12 larger, shifted left, sail top cropped in both; frames 13-16 boat moves back right and runs off the right edge in both (animation 15-16 vs film 15-16). Frame-to-frame changes in the animation are gradual with no pops. But in every animation frame (e.g. 1, 8, 12, 16) the sail is on the right of the mast and the mast stands at the left-middle of the hull, while the film (frames 1-16) and the doodle c.png both put the sail on the left of the mast with the mast toward the right of the hull; the whole drawing has been mirrored. In frames 13-16 the hull also becomes much longer and flatter than in frames 1-4, so its proportions change more than the film's barge does. The two grey background boats at left are static in all 16 frames while the film's horizon traffic changes from steamships (1-4) to sailboats appearing (5-16).
primary_gap: The doodle is drawn mirrored left-to-right, so the sail sits right of the mast and the sail mass occupies the opposite side of the frame from both the film's sail and the doodle's own orientation.
closes_when: In all 16 frames the sail is drawn on the left side of the mast, with the mast standing over the right part of the hull and the hull's raised end stroke on the right, matching c.png and the film's sail placement.
protect: The film-matched path (right of center, drift left by frames 9-12, back right and off the right edge in 14-16), the gradual growth in scale, sail-top cropping from frame 9, the doubled-stroke mast and open-ended hull strokes from the doodle, the plain grey horizon and dashes, and the absence of jumps between frames.
